clue.text: 50p? Heads or tails called for match

parts.note: a 50p piece is a British coin

indicators.note: called means spoken aloud, so the sound of the word is used, not its spelling

parts.note: heads and tails are each a side of a tossed coin

explanation.surface: Someone tosses a 50p coin and calls heads or tails to decide who starts a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads or tails' gives SIDE, which 'called' turns into the same-sounding CIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To coincide is to agree or correspond exactly, a verb synonym of match.

clue.text: Inexperienced medic turned up in maritime conflict

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: raw means green, inexperienced
doc is short for doctor

explanation.surface: A junior doctor finds themselves at sea in the middle of a naval clash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses RAWDOC, written upwards in the grid. The Cod Wars were fishing-rights disputes between Britain and Iceland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cod War was a series of fishing disputes fought at sea between British and Icelandic vessels.

clue.text: Between the sheets, cuddling Romeo; too much Montague blood?

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: having too much of one family's blood, from close intermarriage

indicators.note: cuddling means holding something close inside, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: between the sheets is a euphemism for being in bed
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo in bed with Juliet, and a jibe about the Montague family's bloodline.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: Romeo is a Montague, and a family marrying among itself has too much of its own blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Inbred describes offspring of closely related parents, whose ancestry comes overwhelmingly from one family.

clue.text: Possibly old-fashioned senior ministers making a spirited display

parts.note: an Old Fashioned is a whisky cocktail; possibly marks it as an example
the Cabinet is the group of senior government ministers

explanation.surface: Fusty senior ministers putting on a lively show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' looks like a jibe at the ministers but names a drink. 'Spirited' puns on spirits, the drinks kept in the piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: This furniture item stores and shows off bottles of spirits, so it is literally a display of spirits.

clue.text: Training session in which the players look the part

definitions.text: Training session in which the players look the part

parts.words: Training session in which the players look the part
parts.note: reads like sport practice where the team looks competent, but describes the final theatre run-through done in full costume

explanation.surface: A sports practice where the team at least looks the part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' and 'Training session' suggest sport; the players are actors, who look the part because they are in costume.
explanation.definitionFit: The final rehearsal before opening night is performed in full costume, so the actors visibly appear as their characters.

clue.text: Caught by tracer bullet? That's bitter

indicators.note: caught by means held within the following words, whose letters contain the answer

explanation.surface: Someone hit by tracer fire comments that it is a bitter experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rarer form of acerbic, meaning sour or sharp-tasting, hence bitter.

clue.text: Manufacturing that Tesla micro just in time

indicators.note: manufacturing means building something new, so these letters are put together in a fresh order

parts.note: micro means tiny, as does minute

explanation.surface: A Tesla small car being built only just in time for a deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manufacturing' rearranges THATTESLA into ATTHELAST; 'micro' is a synonym, not part of the anagram, even though it looks like a car model.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at the eleventh hour means getting it done only barely before the deadline.

clue.text: Digging up former husband, upper-class member of the Campbell clan

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-partner
U is the old British label for upper-class usage
Sir Menzies 'Ming' Campbell, a former Liberal Democrat leader, is a Campbell

explanation.surface: Raking up an ex-husband's past as a posh Scottish aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: MING is the nickname of Menzies Campbell, a Scottish politician who led the Liberal Democrats; 'Campbell clan' invites a Highland Scot of any name.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhuming is removing a buried body from the ground, which is literally unearthing it.

clue.text: University accommodation erected in top capital location

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the word for top

parts.note: best means top, finest

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means put up, so the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or place to live

explanation.surface: Student housing put up in a prime city-centre spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' reverses PAD to DAP; U plus DAP goes 'in' BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital city of Hungary, so it is a place that serves as a capital.

clue.text: He authorises US involvement in espionage work

indicators.note: involvement suggests things rolled or tangled together, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A spymaster signs off on American participation in a covert operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involvement' rearranges HEAUTHORISESUS. The Russia House is a John le Carré spy novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russia House is a John le Carré spy novel, so it is a literary work about espionage.

clue.text: At last Vince Cable is sacked following democratic fiasco

indicators.note: following says the shuffled part comes after the letter for democratic

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat or democratic

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the next word
sacked suggests turned upside down and ransacked, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Vince Cable, Liberal Democrat leader, finally loses his job after a party disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' takes E from Vince; 'is sacked' rearranges CABLE into BACLE. Vince Cable was a British Liberal Democrat leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a humiliating collapse or failure, a close synonym for a disastrous fiasco.

clue.text: Henry longed to be married

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance
itched means yearned or longed, as in itching to go

explanation.surface: Henry wanted desperately to get married.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting hitched is informal slang for getting wed, so hitched is a casual synonym.

clue.text: Broker runs out of silver

indicators.note: out of here means the following letter is dropped from the word for silver

parts.note: argent is silver, especially in heraldry
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A dealer has run out of silver to sell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broker' looks like a description of someone trading silver; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts on behalf of others in deals, just as a broker negotiates between buyer and seller.

clue.text: Urban plan encounters pitfall, Spooner reports

indicators.note: Spooner was famed for swapping the opening sounds of words; reports says his version is heard

parts.note: meets means encounters
a trap is a pitfall or snare

explanation.surface: A town planning scheme runs into a hidden snag.
explanation.walkthrough: MEETS TRAP is said as 'meet strap'; swapping the opening sounds M and STR gives 'street map'.
explanation.definitionFit: A street map is a chart of a town's roads, so it is literally a plan of an urban area.

clue.text: Mob assembling — it's a jungle, Elysées evacuated

indicators.note: assembling means putting parts together, so these letters are rearranged
evacuated means emptied, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: A crowd gathers on the Champs-Elysées, chaos reigns and the street is cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembling' rearranges ITSAJUNGLE into GILETSJAUN; 'evacuated' empties Elysées to ES. The gilets jaunes were French yellow-vest protesters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gilets Jaunes were a French protest movement whose crowds filled Paris streets, a protesting mob.

clue.text: Some guffaw at erratic swimmer

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A burst of loud laughter at a swimmer's wild style.
explanation.definitionFit: The water vole, a riverbank rodent, is often called by this name and swims well.

clue.text: Reportedly conned Stallone to host glam BBC show

indicators.note: to host means to hold another piece inside, as a host holds guests

parts.note: Sylvester Stallone's nickname is Sly

indicators.note: reportedly means heard rather than read, so the sound of the word is used

parts.note: tricked means conned, deceived

explanation.surface: Sylvester Stallone was hoodwinked into presenting a glitzy television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Come Dancing is the BBC's ballroom-dancing contest, known for sequins and glamour.
explanation.definitionFit: Strictly is the common short name for Strictly Come Dancing, the sequinned BBC ballroom competition.

clue.text: Provided piece FT carried: "May finally shows a way out of EU"

parts.note: an article is a piece of writing in a newspaper

indicators.note: carried means held inside, so one piece sits within the newspaper initials

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
if means provided, on condition that

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the name

explanation.surface: A newspaper story reports Theresa May's plan for leaving the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried' puts the condition word inside the newspaper's initials. Article 50 of the Treaty on European Union sets out how a member state leaves; Theresa May triggered it.
explanation.definitionFit: Article 50 is the treaty clause under which a member state formally withdraws, which Britain triggered for Brexit.

clue.text: Incredible six-pack seen on Purdy when stripped

parts.note: a six-pack is a set of well-defined abdominal muscles, or abs

indicators.note: stripped means its outer covering is removed, leaving the middle letters

explanation.surface: Someone called Purdy takes their top off to show off impressive abdominal muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' peels the outer letters off PURDY, leaving URD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absurd is so ridiculous it cannot be believed, the sense of unbelievable.

clue.text: English team was first to be banished

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team
led means was in front, was first

explanation.surface: England's side was the first to be sent home from a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: Exiled means expelled from one's own country, which is to be banished.

clue.text: Hired gun running amok round British city

indicators.note: round means placed around, so the shuffled letters surround the letter for British
running amok means wild and out of control, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A hitman goes on the rampage around a British city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running amok' turns HIREDGUN into EDINURGH, which goes 'round' B.
explanation.definitionFit: Edinburgh is the capital city of Scotland, so it is an instance of a city.

clue.text: At home, beginning to browse old Times file

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: Relaxing at home, browsing an old copy of The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is not the newspaper here but the multiplication sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: An inbox is a tray or folder where incoming documents are kept, a kind of file.

clue.text: Building right over frozen land, river having melted

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right, and O the cricket abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: having melted says the letter has disappeared, as ice does, from the word for frozen land

parts.note: tundra is the frozen treeless land of the Arctic

explanation.surface: A tale of the Arctic: a thaw, frozen ground and a river breaking up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, usually topped with a dome, so it is a type of building.

clue.text: That's odd; half of Lausanne retired after sun-up, naked

indicators.note: after says the turned piece follows the trimmed sun-up
naked means stripped of its outer layer, so the outside letters go
retired means went back, so these letters are written in the opposite direction
half of takes the first half of the city's name

explanation.surface: Someone in Lausanne goes to bed just after sunrise, without clothes, which is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' gives LAUS, which 'retired' turns into SUAL; 'naked' strips SUNUP to UNU.
explanation.definitionFit: Unusual means not normal or out of the ordinary, the same as strange or peculiar.

clue.text: Stormy isn't regularly taken out for a secret lovers' meeting

indicators.note: regularly taken out means every other letter is removed, leaving the even letters

explanation.surface: Despite the bad weather having eased, a clandestine romantic rendezvous goes ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the first, third and other odd letters of STORMYISNT leaves T, R, Y, S, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a private arranged rendezvous, typically between sweethearts.

clue.text: Having improved Centre Court, changed winning forecasts

definitions.meaning: having sown fresh grass again on Wimbledon's main court
having altered the tennis seedings, the official ranking of who is expected to win

explanation.surface: Wimbledon groundsmen fix the court while officials rejig the tournament favourites.
explanation.walkthrough: Centre Court is Wimbledon's main grass court; seeds in tennis are top players ranked in advance to keep them apart in the draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses suit the tennis setting: grass sown afresh, and tournament seedings redrawn.
